newsitem.title: GERMANY: Major German firms need global logistic strategies.
newsitem.headline: Major German firms need global logistic strategies.

text.p: Large German companies should seek to develop global logistic strategies to take account of the increasingly global nature of production and sales, Dr Hanspeter Stabenau, chairman of the German shippers association (BVL) said.

The three day BVL annual congress under the slogan "Global tendency" showed industry accepted the need to expand transport planning beyond Germany as increasing numbers of firms opened branches across the world, he told Reuters in an interview.
"The priority should be to think beyond the company and no longer just the success of individual areas of operations but in terms of processing chain," he said.

Stabenau said the subject of information and communications systems for the logistics industry was likely to be the main subject of the next congress, which takes place in Berlin from October 22-24, 1997.
"We have seen the multi-cultural element was raised in many workshops and there is a need to look at this subject. That is what I see as the most important result of this congress," he added.

Rainer Thieme, managing director of automobile parts supplier Wilhelm Karmann GmbH, said in a presentation that German companies needed to develop a far better understanding of Asian culture and society in order to be successful in business there.

Korea, for example, was developing large ship-building capacity to enable it to compete for long-term market share with Japan, which had dominated its Asian neighbours for centuries, he explained to BVL delegates.

Karmann, which assembles imported cars in Germany for Korean manufacturer Kia, saw Asia as the next area of expansion following projects in Mexico and South Africa with Volkswagen, and in Brazil with Ford, Thieme said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
